words.meaning: To intensely dislike or hate something or someone.
words.example: She truly abhors any form of injustice.

words.meaning: A feeling of intense dislike or hatred.
words.example: His abhorrence for violence was evident.

words.meaning: Causing a feeling of intense dislike or hatred.
words.example: Discrimination is abhorrent to a civilized society.
The sudden noise left her feeling alarmed.
The rise in crime rates is alarming.

words.meaning: Showing selfless concern for the well-being of others.
words.example: His altruistic actions benefited the entire community.

words.meaning: A deep-seated feeling of dislike or aversion.
words.example: His antipathy towards modern art was well-known.

grammar.title: Inversion After Negative Adverbials
grammar.explanation:
When a sentence starts with a negative or limiting word like **never**, **rarely** or **hardly**, we use question word order: the auxiliary comes before the subject. This pattern is called **inversion**.

**Inversion** is formal and emphatic. It is common in writing, speeches and storytelling.

If there is no auxiliary, add **do**, **does** or **did**. With **be**, just put **be** first.

With **only when**, **only after** and **not until**, the **inversion** happens in the main clause, not in the first part.

Remember the pairs: **no sooner** goes with **than**, and **hardly** or **scarcely** go with **when**.
examples: ***Never have I** felt so proud.* (never + present perfect)
***Rarely do** we get snow in April.* (rarely + do)
***Seldom has** the city looked so beautiful.* (seldom)
***Hardly had** the match started **when** it began to rain.* (hardly… when)
***No sooner had** she left **than** he arrived.* (no sooner… than)
***Not only is** the hotel cheap, **but** it's also very comfortable.* (not only… but)

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: I have never felt such abhorrence for a cruel act.
practice.a: Never have I felt such abhorrence for a cruel act.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: We rarely see such altruistic kindness in daily life.
practice.a: Rarely do we see such altruistic kindness in daily life.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: She realised only when she got home that the news was alarming.
practice.a: Only when she got home did she realise that the news was alarming.

practice.q: Rewrite using not only: He was alarmed. He also felt antipathy towards the plan.
practice.a: Not only was he alarmed, but he also felt antipathy towards the plan.
